items.description: A Marshall-style all-tube 18-watt amp head with two channels, built from a Mojotone 18 Watt TMB kit in a 19.75" head cabinet I hand-built for it. Fully built, tested, and gig-ready. Channel one is the classic 1974-style 18-watt circuit with big JTM 45-like tones. Channel two is a JCM 800-style lead channel with Treble, Mid, Bass and Master Volume controls. Cathode-biased, two EL84s, EZ81 rectifier. It is loud. Local buyers are welcome to come play it before buying.
items.note: Amp head only. The speaker cabinet in some photos is not included.

items.description: A hand-carved A-style mandolin from Flatiron's Bozeman, Montana shop (pre-Nashville), made in 1994 and signed on the label by Bruce D. Weber. Gibson bought Flatiron in 1987 and kept the Bozeman luthiers building Gibson and Flatiron mandolins there until 1996, when production moved to Nashville. Weber ran that shop and went on to found Weber Fine Acoustic Instruments. The Artist was the top of Flatiron's A-model line: carved spruce top, flamed maple back and sides, bound ebony fingerboard, gold hardware and the pearl-inlaid "The Flatiron" headstock. Bozeman-era Flatirons are well regarded for their tone and are often compared to Gibson A-5s from the same shop. There is no finish checking, and the frets show normal light wear. It has a K&K Mandolin Twin pickup installed, so it plugs straight into an amp or PA through the 1/4" endpin jack, and it comes in its original hard-shell case.
specs: 1994, Bozeman, Montana; label signed by Bruce D. Weber
Maple neck; bound ebony fingerboard with extension and pearl dots
Bound, black face, pearl "The Flatiron" script and fern inlay
Gold engraved 4-on-a-plate tuners, engraved gold tailpiece
K&K Mandolin Twin transducer (passive), standard 1/4" endpin jack

items.description: A very lightly used stereo matched pair of Microphone Parts SDC-84 small-diaphragm condenser mics, with almost no signs of use. I bought them pre-built and factory-matched from Microphone Parts, so this is not a home kit build. They are the company's take on the classic Neumann KM84. Each mic uses a JFET impedance converter and an output transformer, with a capsule designed to follow the KM84's. Sound On Sound's review called the SDC-84 "sonically very close to the real thing" and said that on many sources the reviewer couldn't tell it from his KM84s in a blind test. The two 8 pF pad capacitors are included but not installed, so you can choose: leave them out and the mics are about 15 dB more sensitive than a KM84, good for acoustic guitar, strings and other quiet sources, or install them for KM84-level output on drum overheads and louder sources. A comparable new pair currently sells for $1,099.
specs: Two SDC-84 mics, two shock-mount clips, aluminum flight case
Two 8 pF pad capacitors, spare elastic bands for the clips, mic stand thread adapters, three spare case screws

items.condition: Used, works fine, light wear on the finish

photos.alt: Fishman Pocket Blender, angled front view with the battery door on top
Front panel: microphone and transducer channels with volume, bass, treble, trim and phase, plus master and mute
Back panel: input with phantom power switch, effects loop send and return jacks, 1/4" and XLR outputs, ground lift

items.description: Fishman's original Pocket Blender, the made-in-USA two-channel preamp for blending an acoustic instrument's pickup with a microphone. Each channel has its own volume, bass, treble, trim and phase controls, and the microphone channel adds hi and lo switches. A master volume and mute switch handle the combined signal. Both sources come in on one stereo 1/4" jack (pickup on the tip, mic on the ring), with a switchable 9V supply to power a mini mic. Each channel has its own effects send and return, so you can put a pedal on the pickup or the mic alone. The blend goes out through a 1/4" jack or an XLR with ground lift, so it doubles as a DI into a PA or recording interface. It runs on a 9-volt battery, with a low-battery light on the front, or an AC adapter. Fishman no longer makes it. It works fine; I'm only selling it because I've moved on to other gear.
specs: Two-channel acoustic preamp, blender and DI
Microphone and transducer: volume, bass, treble, trim and phase on each; hi and lo switches on the mic channel
Master volume, mute switch, low-battery light
Stereo 1/4" (transducer on tip, microphone on ring), switchable 9V mic power
Separate send and return for each channel
9V battery or AC adapter (Fishman 910-R or Roland PSA series, per the back panel)
